name: Congenital Optic Disc Excavation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Optic Disc Excavation

criteria.description: Presence of a well-demarcated excavation or pit in the optic nerve head observed on fundoscopic examination
Characteristic visual field defects such as arcuate scotomas or enlarged blind spots
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) or fundus photography confirming excavation morphology and absence of acquired optic neuropathy
No evidence of optic disc swelling or inflammatory signs to exclude optic neuritis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of optic disc excavation on fundoscopic exam confirmed by imaging plus characteristic visual field defects, with exclusion of acquired optic neuropathies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely indicated.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible excavation on optic nerve head
searchTerms: optic disc pit present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Enlarged blind spot on visual field testing
searchTerms: enlarged blind spot on vision test

common.notes: Often detected incidentally during routine eye exams

occasional.notes: May cause visual distortion or decreased acuity
Visual distortion related to macular involvement

rare.notes: Rare complication due to structural abnormalities

imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing optic disc excavation and associated retinal changes
Fundus photography demonstrating optic disc pit
Visual field testing revealing enlarged blind spot and arcuate defects
other: Absence of inflammatory markers or optic nerve swelling

distinguishingFeatures: Larger, more irregular excavation involving the optic disc
Often bilateral and associated with systemic anomalies
Progressive optic nerve cupping with elevated intraocular pressure

redFlags: Sudden onset of visual loss indicating possible serous macular detachment
references: Miller NR. Congenital optic disc anomalies. In: Walsh & Hoyt's Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology. 6th ed. 2005.
Shields JA, et al. Optic disc pits and associated maculopathy. Ophthalmology. 1984.
